title: DFJ12 9-round AES-256 / aes256-9r-single-chosen-key-streamed-dfj2012

target.description: 9 nonlinear AES-256 rounds; Figures 4/9 include the final public linear output map and the subspace condition is transported through it. Figure 1/source Section 2 use AK before SB. This pair-finding endpoint is not unknown-master-key recovery.

setting.key_relation: One freely chosen AES-256 master key used for BOTH messages. No key difference or related-key oracle; the key schedule is standard.
setting.plaintext_model: Construct (m,m-prime,k) such that m XOR m-prime lies in the prescribed four-byte-dimensional input subspace and the ciphertext difference lies in the prescribed four-byte-dimensional output subspace.
assumptions: The adversary chooses one key; not a fixed known-key game and not a secret-key recovery game.

Reduced-round source uses AK before SB and a public linear terminal map. The finite AppendixA witness matches with terminalMC and finalARK; the AppendixB absolute End row has a separate local discrepancy, while its output difference matches.
setting.reference_model: Single-chosen-key limited-birthday restricted-pair construction versus an ideal keyed permutation; source generic comparator 2^64 basic operations.

time.note: Native construction/list cost, not AES encryption equivalents.

success.description: No numerical complete chosen-key distinguishing success is stated for this nine-round AES256 streamed endpoint. The source expects2^24 middle solutions and invokes the earlier storage trick, but does not give a complete output-count or ideal-game decision distribution. Keep the two local key-consistency models separate; do not transfer an AES128 witness or its seven-round list percentage to this endpoint.

components.description: Section4.3: the L0 candidate determines two bytes k4[1,13] shared with L3; the source list model uses a16-bit consistency condition. This is per fixed candidate, not the probability the merged list is nonempty.
Section4.3 Equations12–13: a fixed L1 candidate meets the two named byte conditions under the source model. Expected one match per joined element is not a guarantee of acquisition or uniqueness.

review.scope: Exact-edition targeted success audit. Conditional list/outbound events, one-sided AES acceptance, quartet probabilities and expected q outputs remain distinct from whole-game decision success. Existing scientific conflicts, source versions, native budgets, targets, settings, parameter membership and full-audit gates are unchanged.
